newsitem.title: FRANCE: Olivetti in talks with Fr Telecom - paper.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti in talks with Fr Telecom - paper.

text.p: France Telecom and Italy's Olivetti group are in talks to forge a new strategic alliance that could lead to the French state telephone monopoly buying an equity stake in the troubled Italian company, the International Herald Tribune reported on Monday.
The Paris-based newspaper quoted unnamed executives close to the discussions for the report.
The newspaper said Michel Bon, president of France Telecom, had confirmed in an interview that the two companies were exploring the possibility of a "broader alliance".

At present, France Telecom and Olivetti have plans to cooperate in the Italian telephone market and are working to finalise plans for the French company to make an investment in Infostrada, Olivetti's fixed telephone venture in Italy.
Bon said that any developments concerning Olivetti's overall share capital were of "the utmost interest" to France Telecom.
But the newspaper said he declined to give any details of the current negotiations and would not say whether the talks included the prospect of France Telecom buying a block of Olivetti shares.
But the newspaper quoted what it said were well-placed financial sources who indicated that the idea of a share purchase was being explored.

The newspaper said the possible deal suggested the shape of what could be a wide-ranging reorganisation of Olivetti, focusing on expanding its push into telecommunications and possibly selling its loss-making personal computer division.
